subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing cadence guardrail for recurring cron jobs, with unset/0 preserving shipped behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast schedules?
rationale: This adds a new core config surface and deliberate configured fail-closed behavior for recurring schedules, which is a product and compatibility choice even though the implementation is default-off.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
options.body: Keep the core config surface, require the docs-map/rebase fix and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Narrow To Advisory Behavior
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and use a warning-only path if maintainers want no configured schedule rejection.

options.title: Defer The Config Surface
options.body: Pause this PR and keep the broader cron guardrail work under the existing umbrella until a fuller policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep the core config surface, require the docs-map/rebase fix and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.
